'''''Send Help''''' is a 2026 American [[survival horror film]]<ref>{{Cite web|title='Send Help' - Review|url=https://scriptmag.com/send-help-review|website=Script Magazine|date=2026-01-30|access-date=2026-02-01|language=en|first=Rahul|last=Menon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260216035717/https://scriptmag.com/send-help-review|archive-date=February 16, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> directed and co-produced by [[Sam Raimi]] and written by [[Mark Swift and Damian Shannon|Damian Shannon and Mark Swift]]. The film stars [[Rachel McAdams]] and [[Dylan O'Brien]] as an employee and her boss, respectively, who become stranded on a desert island after a plane crash and attempt to survive while tension rises between them.

''Send Help'' premiered at the [[Grauman's Chinese Theatre|TCL Chinese Theatre]] in Los Angeles, California on January 21, 2026, and was released in the United States by [[20th Century Studios]] on January 30. The film received positive reviews from critics and grossed $94 million against a $40 million production budget.

==Plot==
Socially awkward and downtrodden corporate strategist Linda Liddle anticipates a long-promised promotion from Bradley Preston, the son of her former boss, upon his appointment as CEO. Instead, Bradley awards the position to Donovan, a recent hire and former fraternity brother, and plans to sideline Linda in a dead-end role, citing her unattractiveness and lack of charisma.

When Linda confronts him, Bradley, purporting to be impressed by her boldness, invites her to accompany him, Donovan, and other executives on a business trip to [[Bangkok]] so she can help finalize a company merger. During the flight, Donovan humiliates Linda by playing her audition tape for ''[[Survivor (American TV series)|Survivor]]''. As the plane passes through a storm, it suffers engine failure and rapid altitude loss. During explosive decompression, Donovan attempts to strangle Linda and take her seat, but she stabs him with a fork. Everyone except Linda and Bradley are sucked from the aircraft before it crashes into the sea.

The next morning, Linda washes up on a remote island in the [[Gulf of Thailand]] and finds Bradley alive but badly injured. With no other survivors, Linda builds shelter and secures food and water. Bradley relies on her but continues to treat Linda as a subordinate. In response, Linda abandons him for two days. When she returns, Bradley is near collapse from dehydration. Though still resentful, he begins to accept her authority. Linda proves adept at survival, catching fish and killing a wild boar. While exploring the far side of the island, she avoids signalling a passing boat.

As Bradley recovers, Linda teaches him survival skills but warns him about the far side of the island, claiming it is filled with poisonous plants. One night, while drinking homemade fruit wine, she confesses that she once allowed her abusive husband to drive drunk, leading to his death. Bradley appears sympathetic and offers to cook for Linda, but he poisons her meal with berries so he can escape on a makeshift raft. However, waves destroy the raft, and Linda, having survived, rescues Bradley.

In retaliation, Linda temporarily paralyzes Bradley with [[Greater blue-ringed octopus|octopus toxin]] and pretends to castrate him, asserting control over him and their situation. While harvesting fruit, Linda encounters Bradley's fiancée, Zuri, who arrives by boat after the end of official rescue efforts. Fearing the loss of her new life and purpose, Linda leads Zuri and the boat captain to an unstable cliff, where they fall off. She returns to the camp alone, shaken and withdrawn, allowing Bradley to hunt by himself. While doing so, Bradley discovers Zuri's buried remains.

Confronted, Linda claims the deaths were accidental, but Bradley accuses her of murder and attacks her. In the ensuing fight, Bradley injures Linda's eye before she stabs him. Bradley escapes and discovers a luxurious beach house on the far side of the island. Linda follows, confessing that she had known about the house since seeing the first boat and that she caused Zuri and the captain to fall. Linda threatens Bradley with an unloaded shotgun, and he pleads for his life, claiming he loves her and wishes to remain on the island. However, Linda notices that Bradley is concealing a weapon before he seizes the shotgun. Linda overpowers and kills him with a golf club.

A year later, a rescued Linda is now a wealthy and beloved celebrity, capitalizing on the attention from being the apparent sole survivor of the crash. At a celebrity golf tournament, Linda promotes a film adaptation of her best-selling memoir and announces her intention to write a self-help book, saying, "No help is coming, so you'd better start saving yourself."<!-- DO NOT REMOVE. === Home media ===
''Send Help'' was released on [[VOD]] on March 24, 2026, and on [[DVD]], [[Blu-ray]] and [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] on April 21, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lammers |first=Tim |title=Sam Raimi's Horror Thriller 'Send Help' Gets Streaming Date |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/timlammers/2026/03/17/sam-raimis-horror-thriller-send-help-gets-streaming-date/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=[[Forbes]]|date=March 17, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sam Raimi's 'Send Help' Hits Digital Next Week, Physical Media in April |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/home-video/3941100/sam-raimis-send-help-hits-digital-next-week-physical-media-in-april/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=[[Bloody Disgusting]]|last=DiVincenzo|first=Alex|date=March 17, 2026}}</ref>

[[Nielsen Media Research]], which records streaming viewership on certain U.S. television screens, reported that ''Send Help'' was the third most-streamed film during the week of May 4–10, generating 427 million minutes of watch time during that period.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=2026-06-04 |title=Streaming Ratings: 'La Brea' Gets a Netflix Bump to the Top of the Charts |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/streaming-ratings-may-4-10-2026-1236614013/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gruenwedel |first=Erik |date=2026-06-05 |title=Nielsen: Former NBC Drama 'La Brea' Topped Weekly Household TV Streaming Through May 10 |url=https://www.mediaplaynews.com/nielsen-former-nbc-drama-la-brea-topped-weekly-household-tv-streaming-through-may-10/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[Media Play News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> [[JustWatch]], a guide to streaming content with access to data from more than 45 million users around the world, announced that ''Send Help'' ranked as the most-streamed film in the United States through May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gruenwedel |first=Erik |date=2026-06-03 |title=JustWatch: HBO Max's 'Euphoria,' Hulu's 'Send Help' Most-Streamed Series, Movie in May |url=https://www.mediaplaynews.com/justwatch-hbo-maxs-euphoria-hulus-send-help-topped-may-most-streamed-series-movie/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[Media Play News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
''Send Help'' grossed $65 million in the United States and Canada, and $29 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $94 million.<ref name="BOM" /><ref name="NUM" />

In the United States and Canada, ''Send Help'' was released alongside ''[[Iron Lung (film)|Iron Lung]]'', ''[[Shelter (2026 film)|Shelter]]'', and ''[[Melania (film)|Melania]]'', and was projected to gross $14–17 million from 3,475 theaters in its opening weekend.<ref name="opening">{{cite magazine|last=Rubin|first=Rebecca|date=January 28, 2026|title=Box Office: Sam Raimi's 'Send Help' Targets $15 Million Debut, 'Melania' Doc Aims for $3 Million Against $40 Million Price Tag|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/send-help-melania-doc-box-office-opening-weekend-projections-1236643287/|access-date=January 28, 2026|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260128183022/https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/send-help-melania-doc-box-office-opening-weekend-projections-1236643287/|archive-date=January 28, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> The film made $7.2 million on its first day, including $2.2 million from Thursday night previews. {{Rotten Tomatoes prose|92|7.4|299|Putting director Sam Raimi's penchant for diabolical mayhem to great use, ''Send Help'' doesn't need any assistance in thrills thanks to a very game Rachel McAdams and Dylan O'Brien along with a viciously clever script.|ref=y|access-date=July 25, 2026}} {{Metacritic film prose|75|40|ref=y|access-date=February 5, 2026}} Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/ |access-date=January 31, 2026 |publisher=[[CinemaScore]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title='Send Help' Settles to $19M+, 'Iron Lung' Healthy $18M+; 'Melania' Still $7M+ Record Docu Debut in Decade – Monday U.S. Box Office Update |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/box-office-iron-lung-send-help-melania-shelter-1236703378/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=January 31, 2026 |access-date=January 31, 2026 |language=en-US |first=Anthony |last=D'Alessandro |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130191225/https://deadline.com/2026/01/box-office-iron-lung-send-help-melania-shelter-1236703378/ |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[IndieWire]]''{{'}}s Alison Foreman gave an A− for the film, and called it "wickedly lovable with the potential to be timeless".<ref>{{cite web |last=Foreman |first=Alison |date=January 26, 2026 |title='Send Help' Review: Sam Raimi Manages the Hell Out of Rachel McAdams' Best Comedy Since 'Mean Girls' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-sam-raimi-1235175473/ |access-date=January 28, 2026 |website=[[IndieWire]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129233535/https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-sam-raimi-1235175473/ |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Michael Phillips (critic)|Michael Phillips]] of the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' wrote, "At its simplest, we have here a performance showcase for O'Brien's artfully restrained sniveling and, especially, for McAdams' miraculous shape-shifting abilities. Essentially, ''Send Help'' is ''[[Cast Away]]'' if Wilson the volleyball was a misogynist tool."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/entertainment/movies-tv/article/send-help-review-21311558.php |title='Send Help' review: Rachel McAdams saves Sam Raimi's grisly 'Survivor' riff |last=Phillips |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Phillips (critic) |newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=January 30, 2026}}</ref> [[Frank Scheck]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' wrote, "It could be said that ''Send Help'' indulges in more baroque plot twists than fully necessary and begins to lose some steam toward the end. But the surprising climax, plus an amusing coda, brings it all home. Audiences are in for quite a ride."<ref>{{cite web |last=Scheck |first=Frank |author-link=Frank Scheck |date=January 26, 2026 |title='Send Help' Review: Rachel McAdams and Dylan O'Brien Face Off in Sam Raimi's Rivetingly Bonkers Survival Thriller |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien-sam-raimi-1236481704/ |access-date=January 28, 2026 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129234026/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien-sam-raimi-1236481704/ |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]''{{'}}s Pete Hammond wrote, "''Send Help'' is the first movie gem of 2026, a devilish treat and welcome respite from the real world. It's a pleasure."<ref>{{cite web |last=Hammond |first=Pete |date=January 26, 2026 |title='Send Help' Review: Rachel McAdams Turns The Tables on Boss Dylan O'Brien in Sam Raimi's Delicious Genre-Bending Dark Comic Thriller |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien-sam-raimi-1236696378/ |access-date=January 28, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129234213/https://deadline.com/2026/01/send-help-review-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien-sam-raimi-1236696378/ |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Jeannette Catsoulis of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote, "From its cheeky score by the director's frequent collaborator [[Danny Elfman]], to its darkly humorous tone and playfully yucky special effects, the movie is Raimi at his most gleeful and twisted."<ref>{{cite news |last=Catsoulis |first=Jeannette |date=January 30, 2026 |title='Send Help' Review: Beach Wear (and Tear) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/29/movies/send-help-review.html |access-date=May 18, 2026 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

''[[TheWrap]]''{{'}}s Amelia Emberwing wrote that the film is "a story rooted in the exploration of [[human nature]] and exactly who we become if it means survival both in the literal and figurative sense".<ref>{{cite web |title='Send Help': Rachel McAdams Shines in Sam Raimi's Gritty Tale of Survival and Power Dynamics |url=https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/reviews/send-help-review-sam-raimi-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien/ |website=[[TheWrap]] |date=January 26, 2026 |access-date=January 29, 2026 |first=Amelia |last=Emberwing |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129235145/https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/reviews/send-help-review-sam-raimi-rachel-mcadams-dylan-obrien/ |archive-date=January 29, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Meagan Navarro of ''[[Bloody Disgusting]]'' wrote, "''Send Help'' is full of vibrant personality, with all of Raimi's signatures."<ref>{{cite web |title='Send Help' Review – Sam Raimi is Back in Fine Splatstick Form in Survival Thriller Comedy |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/reviews/3931733/send-help-review-sam-raimi-is-back-in-fine-splatstick-form/ |date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=January 30, 2026 |language=en-US |first=Meagan |last=Navarro |website=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260131144239/https://bloody-disgusting.com/reviews/3931733/send-help-review-sam-raimi-is-back-in-fine-splatstick-form/ |archive-date=January 31, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Debate over who to root for===
The film makes the audience question who exactly to root for: Linda Liddle, the bullied and under-appreciated strategist or Bradley Preston, the abrasive and sexist boss who denies Linda's promotion that his late father promised her.

When working on the movie, director Sam Raimi claims that one of his producers advised that "the fact that [Rachel McAdams] has not really played a dark, terrible villain before really sets the audience up to be surprised".<ref>{{cite web|last=Dunn|first=Jack|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/sam-raimi-rachel-mcadams-doctor-strange-send-help-1236655826/|title=Sam Raimi Says Rachel McAdams Was 'Underutilized' in 'Doctor Strange': 'Promised Myself That I Would Work With Her Again' |date=February 6, 2026|access-date=October 5, 2024|work=Variety}}</ref> However, most critics and audiences seemed to be more sympathetic to Linda despite having Bradley's fiancée Zuri and the boat captain fall off an island cliff.

Dylan O'Brien, who plays Bradley, has said he personally would "ride for Linda".<ref>{{cite web|last=Davids|first=Brian|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/send-help-dylan-obrien-ending-1236490219/|title='Send Help' Star Dylan O'Brien Breaks Down His Surprising Take on the Bloody Ending |date=February 2, 2026|access-date=February 2, 2026|work=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> Rachel McAdams, who plays Linda, has said that the ending should make audiences uncomfortable while one of the film's producers Zainab Azizi also appears to be on Linda's side and states "Sam always loves to root for the underdog".<ref>{{cite web|last=Mullally|first=William|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/arts-culture/film-tv/2026/02/03/send-help-ending-explained-rachel-mcadams-on-why-it-should-make-you-uncomfortable/|title=Send Help ending explained: Rachel McAdams on why it should make you uncomfortable |date=February 3, 2026|access-date=February 3, 2026|work=The National News}}</ref> The film's screenwriters Mark Swift and Damian Shannon refer to Linda as an [[anti-hero]] and when asked if audiences should be rooting for her, Mark replied that it's up to the audience.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cairns|first=Bryan|url=https://comicbook.com/movies/feature/send-helps-writers-still-cant-believe-they-got-away-with-some-of-the-dark-horror-exclusive/|title=Send Help's Writers Still Can't Believe They Got Away With Some of the Dark Horror [Exclusive] |date=February 6, 2026|access-date=February 6, 2026|work=ComicBook.com}}</ref> An alternate ending of the film sees Dennis Haysbert's character Franklin trying to blackmail Linda, which led to [[Slash Film]] asking whether the character of Linda is a "good person".<ref>{{cite web|last=Seibold|first=Witney|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/2131271/sam-raimi-send-help-movie-alternate-ending-explained/|title=Sam Raimi's Alternate Send Help Ending Explained |date=March 24, 2026|access-date=March 24, 2026|work=Slash Film}}</ref>
